_comment: DRAFT - not wired into any loader. A coarse rock-class catalog for the lithology layer identified as the blocker in docs/FUTURE_WORK_SCOPING.md SS G1d/G1e. 18 classes, chosen as the smallest set that (a) separates the endowment hosts named in climgen/resources.go, (b) separates karst-forming from non-karst rock for subterranean_potential, and (c) separates soil parent materials that actually move fertility/pH. Every class must be ASSIGNABLE from fields the terrain/hydrology/climate pipeline already computes - see config/drafts/LITHOLOGY_NOTES.md for the per-cell derivation. Numbers are ordinal, not measured: 1.0 = neutral, >1 enriched, <1 depleted. Endowment keys match the affinity names in config/resource_abundance_earthlike.json (iron, copper, leadSilver, gold, gem, placer, coal, oilGas, evaporite, clay, stone).

conventions.hardness: 0-1 mechanical resistance to erosion/abrasion. Drives relief retention and quarry difficulty.
conventions.erodibility: 0-1 rate of loss under a WET climate specifically. Carbonates are hard but chemically erodible; shale is soft and erodible; granite is both hard and durable. Kept separate from hardness on purpose.
conventions.excavatability: 0-1 ease of digging a tunnel/chamber BY HAND and having it stand up. High = soft but self-supporting (tuff, loess, chalk). Low = either too hard (granite) or too collapse-prone (loose alluvium). Feeds subterranean_potential alongside karst.
conventions.permeability: 0-1 bulk fluid transmission. Drives aquifers, cave water supply, oil/gas trapping (a seal is LOW permeability).
conventions.karst_propensity: 0-1 intrinsic dissolution-cave potential, BEFORE climate gating. Must be multiplied by water availability and vadose thickness at use time.
conventions.soil_parent: fertility_delta is an additive nudge in [-0.4,+0.4] applied to climgen soil fertility; ph_tendency is a new diagnostic climgen does not currently have at all.
conventions.endowment_affinity: Multiplier applied to the corresponding affinity in climgen/resources.go before the argmax. Omitted key = 1.0.

classes.name: Basalt province (flood basalt, hotspot shield, ocean floor)
classes.formation_note: Hotspot chains and rift-margin large igneous provinces. Also the default class for oceanic crust.
classes.pseudokarst_note: Lava tubes and fissure caves - real, extensive, and not dissolution. The second-best cave source after limestone.

soil_parent.note: Basalt weathers to the most fertile common soil on Earth; the Deccan/Columbia analogue.

classes.affinity_note: Native/basaltic copper (Keweenaw analogue); agate and zeolite as the gem mode; excellent durable building stone.

classes.name: Volcanic arc andesite and ash
classes.formation_note: The inland volcanic line above a trench - terrain already places these as Arc seeds.

soil_parent.note: Andosols on fresh ash - highly fertile, which is why people farm active volcanoes.

classes.affinity_note: Epithermal gold-silver and polymetallic vein systems - the classic arc signature.

classes.name: Silicic tuff and ignimbrite (caldera fill)
classes.formation_note: Continental hotspot calderas and evolved arc centres; welded ash-flow sheets covering wide low-relief aprons.
classes.excavatability_note: The Cappadocia case: soft enough to carve with hand tools, cohesive enough that the chamber stands unsupported. The single best rock for a DUG (rather than found) underground settlement.
classes.affinity_note: Obsidian and opal as the gem mode; bentonite clay; soft dimension stone.

classes.name: Granite batholith
classes.formation_note: Exposed where an orogen or old arc has been deeply eroded - requires high relief history, not current volcanism.

soil_parent.note: Coarse sandy acidic soils; kaolin where deeply weathered.

classes.affinity_note: Pegmatite gems (beryl, tourmaline, topaz), tin-tungsten greisen, and the premier durable building/monument stone.

radiance_host.note: Granite is the most radioelement-rich common rock (accessory U/Th). The stable, boring, long-lived host - underpins 'elder hold' polities.

classes.name: Porphyry stock (subvolcanic arc intrusion)
classes.formation_note: The shallow pluton beneath a former arc volcano, exposed only where the arc has been unroofed. Requires arc proximity AND high relief/erosion - a strict two-condition class, which is why porphyry deposits are rare and clustered in belts.

soil_parent.note: Sulfide oxidation gives acid, metal-loaded ground - locally hostile to crops. A nice negative-space effect: the richest copper country farms badly.

classes.affinity_note: THE copper host. Currently climgen infers copper from generic volcanism, which spreads it far too evenly.

classes.name: Ophiolite / serpentinite (obducted ocean crust)
classes.formation_note: A narrow ribbon along continental collision sutures - slivers of ocean floor caught in the closing. Naturally a thin belt, not a blob.

soil_parent.note: Serpentine barrens: high Mg/Ni, low Ca - genuinely toxic to most crops. The most distinctive soil effect in the catalog and worth having for its own sake.

classes.affinity_note: Cyprus-type massive sulfide copper, chromite, and jade/nephrite as the gem mode.

classes.name: Kimberlite pipe field
classes.formation_note: Only stable ancient cratonic interiors - diamonds need a thick cold keel. Must be assigned as a sparse POINT PROCESS (a handful of small clusters per world), never as a smooth field, or the world drowns in diamonds.
classes.affinity_note: Diamond. Downstream alluvium inherits it as gem-placer - the reason placer should sample upstream lithology.

classes.name: Cratonic basement (gneiss and greenstone belts)
classes.formation_note: Ancient continental interior far from every active boundary, planed to low relief. The default land class for old continental cores.

soil_parent.note: Thin, leached, ancient. Shield country farms poorly and always has.

classes.affinity_note: Orogenic (greenstone-belt) gold - a LOWLAND gold province, which the current mountain-biased gold rule cannot produce at all.

classes.name: Banded iron formation
classes.formation_note: Ancient chemical sediment now within cratonic basement. Like kimberlite, a sparse patch process seeded on craton cells - but larger patches (a whole iron range, not a pipe).
classes.affinity_note: The single largest correction available. Real bulk iron is BIF on old shields, not alpine peaks.

classes.name: Orogenic schist and slate belt
classes.formation_note: Regionally metamorphosed sediment in a mountain belt - the bulk fill of a young orogen.
classes.affinity_note: Orogenic quartz-vein gold; garnet/corundum; roofing slate, which is a distinct and valuable stone good.

classes.name: Marble and metacarbonate belt
classes.formation_note: A carbonate platform caught in a later collision - assign where a mountain belt overprints cells that would otherwise score as limestone_platform. Derivable from ordering: platform first, orogeny second.
classes.karst_note: Marble karsts readily and does it in HIGH RELIEF, which produces deep vertical cave systems rather than shallow flat ones - the strongest subterranean sites in the catalog when combined with orogenic elevation.
classes.affinity_note: Skarn iron/copper at intrusive contacts; ruby/spinel in marble (Mogok analogue); premier sculptural stone.

classes.name: Limestone / dolomite platform
classes.formation_note: Warm shallow shelf on a tectonically quiet continental margin - far from any active boundary, near the coast, low relief, low latitude. This is a clean derivation and it produces belts in the right places.
classes.karst_note: The canonical cave rock. Note permeability is secondary (conduit, not matrix) - surface streams vanish, which is itself a settlement-relevant fact: karst plateaus are water-poor on top and water-rich below.

soil_parent.note: Thin, droughty, alkaline rendzina - modest fertility but distinctive pH, which gates crops that climgen currently cannot express.

classes.affinity_note: Mississippi-Valley-type lead-zinc: a LOWLAND silver province on flat carbonate country. Plus building limestone and lime for mortar - a structural input the trade layer wants.

classes.name: Continental sandstone and redbeds
classes.formation_note: Coarse clastic fill shed off uplifts into an adjacent basin, under an arid to seasonal climate.
classes.pseudokarst_note: Sandstone alcoves and slot systems - shallow shelters, not deep systems. The cliff-dwelling case.
classes.affinity_note: Redbed (stratabound) copper - a sedimentary copper province with no volcanism anywhere near it, which the current volcanism-keyed copper rule cannot produce. Aquifer sandstone is also the desert-oasis mechanism.

radiance_host.note: Richest where sandstone rests directly on craton_basement (unconformity type) - a two-class adjacency rule, so these sites are rare, findable, and worth fighting over.

classes.name: Marine shale and mudstone basin
classes.formation_note: Fine clastic fill in a subsiding, water-covered or recently water-covered basin.
classes.excavatability_note: Soft to dig but squeezes and slumps - low, not high, subterranean value. Seals aquifers and hydrocarbons.

soil_parent.note: Heavy clay soils: fertile but hard to work with a light plough - a good hook for the agriculture/labour layer.

classes.affinity_note: The hydrocarbon source rock and the pottery clay supply in one class.

classes.name: Coal measures (cyclothem swamp sequence)
classes.formation_note: Subsiding basin under a warm, wet, forested regime. climgen already computes precisely this climate gate for coal - lithology adds the missing requirement that a sedimentary basin be there at all.
classes.affinity_note: Blackband/bog ironstone sits inside coal measures - coal and iron co-locate, which is exactly why the two industries did. This co-location is a strong emergent geography and is impossible today.

classes.name: Evaporite basin (halite and gypsum)
classes.formation_note: Restricted or closed basin under aridity - a young rift arm or an endorheic interior. Hydrology already labels terminal sinks and lakes, and climate already gives aridity, so this class is nearly free to assign.
classes.karst_note: Gypsum and salt karst is fast, extensive, and COLLAPSE-PRONE. Good caves, dangerous ground - a natural hazard/instability tag if the settlement layer ever wants one.

soil_parent.note: Saline; compounds the salinity term climgen soil already computes.

classes.affinity_note: Salt is a strategic trade good and a preservation input; salt domes also trap hydrocarbons.

classes.name: Alluvium and basin fill
classes.formation_note: Unconsolidated cover over whatever lies beneath. Should be treated as an OVERLAY: keep the underlying class for the deep/cave and radiance questions, use alluvium for soil and placer.
classes.excavatability_note: Digs easily and collapses immediately below the water table - the worst underground ground in the catalog.
classes.affinity_note: Placer must inherit from the UPSTREAM source class via the hydrology receiver graph, not from the alluvium itself.

classes.name: Loess and windblown regolith
classes.formation_note: Dust blanket downwind of a large arid or glacial source. climgen already has prevailing winds and aridity, so the downwind trace is computable - it just has never been used for this.
classes.excavatability_note: Loess holds a vertical face - the yaodong cave-house case. Cheap shelter, shallow only.

soil_parent.note: The most fertile parent material there is; deep, calcareous, easily tilled.

classes.affinity_note: Contributes almost nothing mineral and a great deal agricultural - a deliberate inverse of the shield classes.

overprints._comment: Not classes. Modifiers applied on top of an assigned class, because they are weathering/cover states rather than rock types, and climgen already computes their drivers.

laterite_duricrust.trigger: soil.Weathering high AND low relief AND wet-tropical
laterite_duricrust.note: Deep tropical weathering profile - laterite/bauxite. Also caps relief and makes hard iron-crust building stone.

glacial_scour.trigger: IceAffinity high or recently high, high latitude/altitude
glacial_scour.note: Strips regolith to bare rock and dumps till elsewhere; also excavates and opens existing karst.

radiance_hook._comment: SS G1e wants radiant minerals as the subterranean primary-energy premise. Hosts are the three classes flagged radiance_host above.
radiance_hook.rule: richness x decay_rate is roughly CONSTANT. A vein is either rich and short-lived or weak and long-lived; nothing is both.

decades.world: prospecting rushes, ghost towns within a lifetime

centuries.world: a full rise-peak-decline arc in recorded history

millennia.world: ancient stable holds - the elder powers

renewing.note: Only at active volcanism - reuses the existing hotspot field, and is the autarkic-vent exception SS G1d already reserves.

radiance_hook.assignment: Sample vein sites as a point process on cells whose class is radiance_host, weighted by rarity; draw the decay band from share_of_veins; set grade from the band. Bonanza sites prefer sandstone_redbed-on-craton_basement unconformities (rare, sharp, findable); millennia sites prefer granite_batholith and silicic_tuff (common, diffuse).
